newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends up on technical adjustments.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends up on technical adjustments.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices were higher at the close, aided by a tight supply of latex and other raw materials, but demand was still weak with most consumers on holiday, traders said.
"There's been no change since last week. The market's still dead," said a trader in Kuala Lumpur.

At the close, the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board (MRELB) quoted January RSS1 buyer at 318.50 cents ($1.26) a kg, up 1.50 cents from Friday. January SMR 20 buyer was quoted one cent higher at 309.50.
A dealer said after Friday's close that he expected both the RSS1 and SMR 20 to appreciate by three to five cents this week.
Traders offered SMR CV at 365 cents, SMR L at 345, SMR 5 at 320, SMR 10 at 310, SMR 20 at 309 and drum latex at 238.

They said producers were holding to current prices because rains were hampering tapping activities at plantations and reducing the flow of latex and processed rubber into the market. Overseas buyers were, meanwhile, on holiday, they said.
The INRO five-day moving average rose to 240.52 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on Dec 13 from 240.32 on Dec 12. The daily indicator price jumped to 241.15 from 240.99.
